articles.title: Parseable API keys inherit role permissions across telemetry streams
articles.excerpt: Parseable API keys inherit role permissions across telemetry streams Parseable stores and queries logs, metrics, traces, and events. It supports native authentication, OIDC, and API keys. The official…
articles.body: Parseable API keys inherit role permissions across telemetry streams Parseable stores and queries logs, metrics, traces, and events. It supports native authentication, OIDC, and API keys. The official API-key documentation says a key is resolved to its roles and then authorized like any other user. The RBAC documentation describes roles such as Admin, Editor, Writer, Reader, and Ingestor, with different access across resource, stream, query, and ingestion endpoints. That design makes a Parseable key a useful integration credential and a meaningful security boundary. A key created for a log shipper should not automatically see every stream, and an OIDC group mapping should not grant more authority than the application expects.
articles.author: SorrelThorncroft

articles.title: The AI Understood My Payment Request. My Rust Code Refused It.
articles.excerpt: An AI that can read "send 0.05 SOL to Ada for lunch" is useful. An AI that can decide to send money is a liability. For the MLH Solana Hackathon, I built SpendGuard, a payment agent for Solana Devnet.…
articles.body: An AI that can read "send 0.05 SOL to Ada for lunch" is useful. An AI that can decide to send money is a liability. For the MLH Solana Hackathon, I built SpendGuard , a payment agent for Solana Devnet. You talk to it in plain English. An LLM turns your words into a payment proposal. Deterministic Rust code then decides whether that payment is allowed. You approve the exact transaction, and only then does anything get signed. Here is the idea in one terminal session: $ spendguard pay "please send 0.05 SOL to ada for lunch" ── Payment sg_dce51019679c ────────────────────────────── To: ada (AVFs2Cd1…yWRWK) Amount: 0.05 SOL Memo: spendguard:sg_dce51019679c Note: lunch (kept locally, not on-chain) Budget: 0.25 SOL left of today's limit after this payment Sign and send this payment?
articles.author: Lymah

articles.title: De la plasticité cérébrale au game design : pourquoi l'entraînement visuel doit devenir un jeu
articles.excerpt: De la plasticité cérébrale au game design : pourquoi l'entraînement visuel doit devenir un jeu Une étude récente rappelle quelque chose d'essentiel : à l'ouverture des yeux, le cerveau connaît une pou…
articles.body: De la plasticité cérébrale au game design : pourquoi l'entraînement visuel doit devenir un jeu Une étude récente rappelle quelque chose d'essentiel : à l'ouverture des yeux, le cerveau connaît une poussée de connexions qui affine en quelques jours les réponses visuelles. Autrement dit, l'expérience visuelle ne décore pas un circuit déjà figé — elle le finit. Pour les personnes atteintes d'amblyopie (lazy eye), cette fenêtre de plasticité n'est pas qu'une curiosité de laboratoire. Elle explique pourquoi la rééducation visuelle fonctionne, et pourquoi elle demande de la répétition, de la régularité et surtout de l'engagement. Le problème, c'est que l'engagement est exactement ce qui manque au cache-œil et aux exercices monoculaires classiques. On isole l'œil faible. On s'ennuie. On arrête.
articles.author: Ashish

articles.body: PDF yang sudah disensor bisa gagal dengan lebih banyak cara daripada sekadar "ada yang menggambar kotak hitam". Kotaknya bisa jadi bagian dari halaman atau berupa anotasi di atasnya, tanda redaksi bisa ditambahkan tapi tidak pernah diterapkan, redaksi bisa diterapkan lalu disimpan secara incremental sehingga halaman lamanya masih ada di dalam file, dan nama penulis bisa tetap tersimpan di metadata sejak awal. Di layar, semuanya terlihat sama persis. Untuk melihat mana yang benar-benar membocorkan data, saya membuat tujuh versi dari formulir satu halaman yang sama, lalu memeriksa masing-masing dengan tiga text extractor (PyMuPDF, pypdf, dan pdfminer.six), scan terhadap setiap stream di dalam file, dan metadatanya.

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 7, 1992: NASA launches Mars Global Surveyor, its 1st Mars mission in 20 years at the time, to map the Red Planet like never before
articles.excerpt: On Nov. 7, 1996, NASA launched its Mars Global Surveyor mission, the first Mars mission in 20 years. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Nov. 7, 1996, NASA launched its Mars Global Surveyor mission. This was the first mission NASA sent to Mars in almost 20 years! The Mars Global Surveyor spacecraft was an orbiter. It transmitted data from NASA's Mars rovers Sojourner , Spirit and Opportunity back to Earth. The spacecraft also did a lot of its own science. It found surface channels on Mars that appeared to have been created by running water. Mars Global Surveyor looked at the south pole of Mars and saw signs of possible climate change. It also saw a mineral called hematite on Mars. Hematite usually forms in water. NASA then sent its Spirit and Opportunity rovers to look for the hematite, and both rovers found it near their landing sites. Mars Global Surveyor survived much longer than expected.

articles.excerpt: NASA is asking the public to send their names to Titan for an ambitious mission that will see a flying craft explore the Saturn moon in 2034, if all goes according to plan.
articles.body: We still may be some time away from sending humans to distant reaches of the solar system, but you can send your name to Saturn's moon Titan, which has the ingredients of life on its surface thanks to NASA's Dragonfly mission. Dragonfly is an SUV-sized nuclear-powered rotorcraft that NASA aims to launch towards Titan in 2028. The agency opened a special events page in late October to allow members of the public to put their name on the spacecraft. The names will be put upon a chip on Dragonfly during the spacecraft's assembly, and all names must be submitted before Jan. 15, 2027. The agency says that the mission has no "ordinary itinerary," as Dragonfly aims to between areas miles (or kilometers) apart after arriving on the surface in 2034.

articles.title: Star Wars is experiencing a golden age of video games
articles.excerpt: The movies might be struggling to recapture the magic, but Star Wars video games are strong with the Force.
articles.body: After a tumultuous start to EA's rebooted Star Wars Battlefront series, in 2021 Lucasfilm and Disney decided to open up the development of new Star Wars games by bringing in different publishers and studios under the Lucasfilm Games banner. Now, over five years on, we can confidently say we're entering a new golden era of amazing Star Wars games . With LucasArts' successor calling the shots and coordinating a multitude of projects set in a galaxy far, far away, even EA's latest efforts like Squadrons and the Jedi series have taken bigger and bolder swings. Now, in 2026, the full potential of the Star Wars universe has become clearer with specific releases squarely aimed at niche audiences.

articles.title: 'I think we will prevail': NASA chief Jared Isaacman on Artemis, China and the new moon race (exclusive)
articles.excerpt: NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman during a a Dec. 3, 2025 confirmation hearing. In October of 2026, Isaacman sat down with Space.com to discuss the future of the space agency.
articles.body: NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman is serious about launching "big rockets" to the moon every single year for the agency's Artemis program. And the new space race with China is fueling that ambition. "I feel good. I feel like we are certainly on a more achievable path to the lunar surface today than where we were before," Isaacman told Space.com. We recently sat down with the NASA chief to discuss the state of the Artemis program , and, off the bat, he made it clear that he's confident in the U.S. space program following the success of April's Artemis II mission around the moon. In fact, just prior to our conversation, it was announced that Artemis II commander Reid Wiseman will become the new deputy director of NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory.
